newsitem.title: USA: South Dakota winter wheat seeding progresses.
newsitem.headline: South Dakota winter wheat seeding progresses.

text.p: Winter wheat seeding and emergence progressed rapidly in South Dakota because of needed rainfall during the week ended Sunday but remained behind year ago and five-year average levels, according to the Agricultural Statistics Service.

Winter wheat was seeded on 53 percent of the acreage, compared with 68 percent a year ago and 70 percent for the average. Fifteen percent of the winter wheat crop had emerged, compared with 23 percent a year ago and the 32 percent average.

Two percent of the corn crop had been harvested for grain, compared with one percent last year and four percent on average. The corn crop was 26 percent mature, compared with 40 percent last year and 48 percent for the average.

Soybean harvesting was rated two percent complete, compared with one percent last year and five percent for the average. Soybeans were mature on 28 percent of the acreage, compared with 22 percent last year and 35 percent average.
Soil moisture conditions were rated three percent very short, 13 percent short, 76 percent adequate and eight percent surplus. There were 3.4 days suitable for fieldwork.
